approach: Multitask Chemprop v2 D-MPNN with CheMeleon pretrained initialization; all 4 direct pIC50 endpoints + both TDI-arm regressions in one model; RDKit/Mordred descriptors concatenated; MPNN LR 1e-4
expected_benefit: Matches the configuration that dominated the top 20 of ExpansionRx (Chemprop in ~15/20, CheMeleon in 8/20, multitask in 18/20) and is the organizers' own stack; sparse-to-dense multitask transfer is the one reproduced gain in the CYP literature
risk: Low. Crowded: PXR top tier held 28 statistically indistinguishable entries, so this alone will not win the regression leaderboard

approach: TDI as shift regression: predict delta = pIC50(+NADPH) - pIC50(direct) continuously, then threshold at 0.301 log units with the operating point tuned to maximize MCC under expected imbalance; direct inhibition as auxiliary task
representation: shared multitask graph+descriptor representation from rank 1
expected_benefit: Retains information a binary 2-fold threshold discards, matches the state of the art (Novartis multitask, prospectively evaluated against assay variability), and MCC is highly sensitive to threshold placement; only four TDI prediction papers exist so the field is thin
risk: Medium. CYP2D6 positive class will be very small (CYP2D6 MBIs are individually characterized rather than compiled); shift labels inherit IC50-shift assay artifacts (fold-shift correlates with kinact/KI at only R2=0.17)

approach: Gradient-boosted descriptor ensemble (XGBoost + LightGBM + CatBoost on RDKit + Mordred + ECFP4) blended with the D-MPNN predictions
expected_benefit: XGBoost beat the multitask deep autoencoder on external CYP test sets (90.4% vs 88.5%); replicated by an independent sweep (GBM AUC 0.92 vs deep 0.89); 3 of ExpansionRx top 10 used hybrid MPNN+classical ensembles
risk: Very low. Marginal gain over rank 1 alone may be within bootstrap noise

approach: Probe-aware ChEMBL/PubChem curation: stratify CYP3A4 records by probe substrate (midazolam vs testosterone vs fluorogenic) and assay technology; pass provenance as feature or separate task; AID 1851 as pretraining signal not label source
expected_benefit: CYP3A4 inhibition is documented as probe-substrate dependent with an allosteric mechanism; pooled ChEMBL injects variance the single-probe test set lacks. Organizers showed mismatched external data actively hurts (MPPB MAE +0.2, R2 < -1.2) while matched surrogate data helps (Caco-2 rho 0.34 -> 0.70)
risk: Low technical risk; benefit is uncertain until the training pack reveals how much external data is even needed
status: proven principle, untested in this challenge

approach: Mechanism-class structural-alert featurization: per-class SMARTS retaining substituent context for acetylene, methylenedioxyphenyl/benzodioxole, thiophene, furan, aniline, hydrazine, thioamide; used as learned features not filter rules
expected_benefit: TDI has genuine mechanistic substructure rules unlike direct inhibition; distinct alert classes map to distinct mechanisms (ketene/oxirene heme alkylation vs carbene MI-complex vs S-oxide). Both published CYP3A4 TDI models recovered alerts post hoc, so supplying them a priori should help a small-data classifier
risk: Low. Quantum-chemical work shows alert reactivity is context-dependent, so a naive binary SMARTS flag underperforms; must preserve substituent context
status: proven chemistry, modest published modeling gains

approach: Interval-aware ST-RAE-matched loss with calibrated uncertainty: predict a predictive distribution per endpoint and place the point estimate to minimize expected distance to the nearest credible-interval bound; conformal or ensemble calibration
expected_benefit: Directly optimizes the actual leaderboard metric rather than MAE; predictions inside the credible interval incur zero error, so a well-calibrated model can bank free score on low-activity compounds where intervals are widest. Organizers report their own CYP3A4 model's median predicted uncertainty is ~5x experimental error, so calibration is demonstrably unsolved
risk: High. The ST-RAE normalization denominator and the credible-interval width/level are unpublished, so the size of the gain cannot be computed before launch; risk of over-engineering against a misunderstood metric

approach: TabPFN v2 in-context learning stacked on frozen CheMeleon embeddings (plus descriptors), per-endpoint
representation: frozen foundation-model embeddings as tabular features
expected_benefit: The exact combination OpenADMET names as the untried next step after their CheMeleon improvement campaign failed; no task-specific training, strong in the low-to-medium data regime, and cheap to try. TabPFN in ExpansionRx was used on raw descriptors, not on foundation-model embeddings
risk: Medium. TabPFN was popular but not top-performing in ExpansionRx; context-length limits constrain how much training data can be used per prediction

approach: On-target pretraining/augmentation over Enamine in-stock and FDA-approved chemical space, optionally with surrogate ADMET pseudo-labels as pretraining targets rather than computed descriptors
expected_benefit: Organizers found a narrow 40k on-target generated set outperformed a 10M maximally diverse set, and that surrogate ADMET pseudo-descriptors were one of only two featurizations giving a net 6% MAE reduction (with MiniMol embeddings); a public 4-task CYP surrogate model covering reversible and time-dependent inhibition exists
risk: Medium-high. Same campaign found CheMeleon largely insensitive to pretraining choices and pretraining loss a poor proxy for fine-tuning performance, so gains may not materialize
